source.title: Scalable Graph Generative Modeling via Substructure Sequences
source.authors: Ze-Hong Wang; Zhe-Yuan Zhang; Tian-Yi Ma; Chu-Xu Zhang; Yanfang Ye

record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling experiments to graph models and reports downstream accuracy as model size and pretraining-data ratio vary; it does not measure language-model cross-entropy or fit the claimed laws.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses language and vision scaling as motivation, but its own scaling results are graph-model linear-probe accuracies. It does not report held-out cross-entropy, power-law fits, large-run extrapolation, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. The model-size and data-ratio outcomes are recorded for V6; other benchmark results are not scaling measurements.
record.test_reason: This is a graph-method paper. It cites Kaplan et al. as motivation and shows that its own G2PM model's linear-probe accuracy rises with hidden size and pretraining-data fraction. It reports no pretraining loss, no power-law fit and no prediction from scaling curves, and the system is a graph Transformer, not a language model. So its results do not bear on any version as worded: V5 needs a power-law form and V6 needs predictability. The sweep is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that G2PM scales with model size and data, unlike message-passing GNNs, which plateau, and they present this as echoing scaling in other domains. They fit no power law and report no loss.
record.recipe_differences: Graph Transformer pretraining with masked substructure reconstruction; evaluates graph-task accuracy rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy and does not perform compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The tested graph datasets and the parameter-size and pretraining-data settings vary; the study reports no fitted-law sensitivity analysis.

fits_no_version.finding: G2PM graph Transformer linear-probe accuracy rises monotonically with hidden dimension (0.4M to 64.5M parameters): 68.2 to 72.3 on ogbn-arxiv, 69.7 to 78.7 on ogbg-HIV. It also improves with pretraining-data fraction. Message-passing baselines (GraphMAE, BGRL) plateau or degrade.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream accuracy of non-language (graph) self-supervised Transformers increases monotonically with model and data scale, without a fitted power-law form.

record.problems: The scaling outcomes are downstream graph-task accuracies, not held-out pretraining loss; the data-ratio values are figure-only; no power-law fits, extrapolation tests, or compute-optimal comparisons are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Other task benchmarks and architecture/augmentation ablations were omitted because they do not measure scaling behavior relevant to the tested downstream-performance version.

untested.parts: No language-model held-out loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No fitted laws and no extrapolation.
No loss comparison of architecture shapes at fixed parameter count. The depth ablation (Fig. 5a) changes parameter count.
Graph-model scale sweeps are reported, but with no loss and no power-law form tested.
No predictive relation between scale or loss and downstream accuracy, and no language models.
No fitting choices or exponents compared.

missing.what: Encoder depth sweep: 1, 2 and 3 encoder layers (about 7.1M, 14.2M and 21.3M parameters) give arxiv 71.1, 72.2, 72.3 and HIV 75.9, 77.6, 78.7. A larger decoder lowers HIV to 71.9.
missing.versions: none (would fit the fits_no_version graph-scaling entry)

missing.what: Baseline scaling curves: GraphMAE and BGRL degrade as parameters or data grow.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T3/V6 'supports' label is dropped. The rows show the method's own accuracy rising in graph tasks, with no predictability or power-law test, and V6/V5 as worded concern predictable or power-law scaling. R11 is redundant with R5.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss or loss-versus-parameter, token, or compute measurements.
No power-law fit on small runs or prediction of larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or parameter/token allocation trend.
No controlled comparison of architecture details at a fixed parameter count for loss.
The study varies graph-model scale, but does not establish that a power-law form holds in another modality or training regime.

Tests graph-model downstream accuracy against model size and pretraining-data ratio, but not language-model performance, downstream performance versus pretraining loss, or predictive fits from scaling curves.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents, compute-optimal splits, or evidence of curves bending away from a power law.
